claim: China's overall share of Apple's supply-chain factory locations has fluctuated around 40% from 2013 to 2023, a far smaller shift than headlines about 'decoupling' suggest, despite India and Southeast Asia gaining share in specific segments.
stance_target: Claim that Apple's supply chain has substantially decoupled from China
scope_conditions: Apple's top-200 suppliers (98% of materials/manufacturing/assembly spend), 2013-2023, by factory location
quoted_support: The total share of factories in China has fluctuated around 40 percent for the duration of our data.

claim: Before 2018, 60-70% of Apple's electronics-manufacturing (final assembly) locations were in China, including nearly all iPhone assembly; today about 50% of assembly locations are in China, but of the 34 assembly facilities still located in China, only 3 are operated by Chinese-owned firms -- the rest are Taiwanese/foreign contract manufacturers.
stance_target: Fast-moving assembly-location diversification is largely relocation of the SAME foreign (Taiwanese) contract manufacturers, not a shift away from the incumbent supplier ecosystem
quoted_support: Before 2018, around 60-70 percent of electronics manufacturing locations were in China, including nearly all final assembly of key devices like iPhones... Today, by contrast, around 50 percent of Apple facilities are in China... Of the 34 electronics manufacturing facilities reported in China, only three are operated by Chinese firms.

claim: Precision manufacturing (machining, tooling, alloy metalworking) has seen the most dramatic shift toward Chinese ownership in Apple's supply chain, with the China-headquartered share of firms in this category rising from 14% in 2013 to 86% in 2023 -- the segment most resistant to non-China diversification.
stance_target: Diversification of deep, tooling/skilled-labor-intensive value-added segments (as opposed to final assembly) is genuinely slow, since precision manufacturing is becoming MORE China-concentrated even as assembly diversifies
quoted_support: This segment has seen the most dramatic shift toward Chinese ownership and Chinese factory location. Nearly all precision manufacturing today occurs in China... In precision manufacturing, China's share of firms by headquarters has increased from 14 percent to 86 percent.

claim: Semiconductors remain overwhelmingly non-Chinese in Apple's supply chain by firm headquarters (63% US-headquartered, only 4% China-headquartered in 2023) even where some chip packaging/assembly occurs on Chinese soil, and PCB suppliers are 88% Taiwan-headquartered with only one Chinese-headquartered firm among ~23 China-located PCB facilities.
stance_target: High-value, technologically complex segments of Apple's value chain remain firmly outside Chinese ownership regardless of factory geography
scope_conditions: Apple semiconductor and PCB supplier categories, 2023
quoted_support: In semiconductors, only 4 percent of Apple suppliers are headquartered in China, and 63 percent are headquartered in the US... In PCBs—a segment for which slightly over half of factories are in China—88 percent of Apple suppliers are headquartered in Taiwan; only one was Chinese.

claim: Analyzing electronics products solely by assembly location is economically misleading for tariff policy, because final assembly typically costs only around $10 per device -- a small fraction of a device's value -- so shifting assembly location alone has minimal supply-chain economic impact.
stance_target: Assembly-location tariffs/policy meaningfully address the underlying (component-level) China exposure of a device like the iPhone
quoted_support: this analysis underscores the futility of analyzing a device solely by where it was assembled—and, as a result, the irrationality of imposing tariffs using this logic... The assembly process for devices like phones often only costs around $10—a tiny fraction of the sales price.

claim: Chinese firms have made the most progress winning business from Apple in lower-tech, lower-margin, commoditized supply-chain segments (e.g. precision manufacturing, commodity materials), while foreign firms retain dominant positions in higher-tech, higher-margin segments (semiconductors, PCBs, specialty materials), even when those firms manufacture inside China.
stance_target: The China-anchored component ecosystem is stratified: value capture by Chinese firms is concentrated in low-margin commoditized work, not high-value IP-intensive segments
quoted_support: Chinese firms have made much more progress winning business with Apple in lower-tech, lower-profit-margin segments of the supply chain, while foreign firms (including those producing in China) generally remain well represented in higher-tech, higher-margin segments of the supply chain.
